note: Real crowd disasters, as sourced descriptions. The Designer agent builds each venue from `description` (the same path as an organizer's sentence); nothing here is geometry. Numbers and sources: docs/REAL_CASES.md.

cases.title: Love Parade 2010 · Duisburg ramp
cases.toll: 21 people died and more than 500 were injured.
cases.description: Open-air access route to the Love Parade festival grounds in Duisburg, Germany, on 24 July 2010 around 16:30. A road tunnel 20 m wide runs west to east under a railway embankment; draw 126 m of it with the ramp in the middle. Its west and east ends are open, 18 m wide: that is where visitors came in and where leaving visitors went out. Halfway along the north wall of the tunnel a single ramp 26 m wide and 130 m long climbs north to the festival grounds; it was the only way in and out. Fences narrowed the middle of the ramp to 10.6 m for about 10 m. A narrow staircase about 1.5 m wide on the west side of the ramp, near its bottom, led up the embankment. The top of the ramp opens onto the festival grounds. 3,000 people: 1,150 arriving in the west half of the tunnel and 1,150 in the east half, all heading up the ramp to the festival grounds, and 700 on the ramp leaving the festival, heading down to the tunnel ends.
cases.what_happened: Arriving and leaving visitors met where the only ramp joined the tunnels; the crowd at the foot of the ramp, near a narrow staircase, became so dense that 21 people were crushed to death.
cases.lesson: One route for both arrivals and departures, with no way to hold the inflow, turns a junction into a crush.

sources.label: Helbing & Mukerji (2012), Crowd disasters as systemic failures: analysis of the Love Parade disaster, EPJ Data Science 1:7
Same paper, open preprint (arXiv:1206.5856): tunnel about 20 m, ramp 26 m by 130 m, 10.59 m usable width, flows per minute

dimensions: Tunnel: smallest width about 20 m (Helbing & Mukerji, citing the city's documents).
Ramp: 26 m wide and 130 m long, the only entrance and exit (ibid.).
Usable ramp width 10.59 m because of two triangular fence structures (G. K. Still's expert report, as summarised by Helbing & Mukerji).
Flows 15:00–15:40: 450–750 people per minute in, 40–250 out (camera 13 analysis, ibid.).
Most victims lay between the narrow staircase and the tunnel entrance, at the foot of the ramp (ibid.).
approximations: Only 126 m of the tunnel is drawn; the real tunnels on both sides were longer.
The ramp is drawn flat; its slope is not simulated.
The staircase width (1.5 m) and the exact place and length of the fences are not published; they are estimates.
3,000 people (the simulation limit) stand for a crowd of tens of thousands; 700 leaving against 2,300 arriving is within the published in/out flow ratio.
Police cordons on the ramp and in the tunnels are not modelled.

cases.title: Hillsborough 1989 · Leppings Lane pens
cases.toll: 97 people died (95 at the time of the Taylor inquiry; the 97th death was ruled unlawful killing in 2021).
cases.description: Standing terrace behind the goal at the Leppings Lane end of Hillsborough stadium, Sheffield, 15 April 1989, just before 3 pm. Two neighbouring pens, pen 4 on the left and pen 3 on the right as seen facing the pitch, together 25 m wide along the pitch and 15 m deep, split by a radial fence running from the back to the front (about 190 m² each). The pitch is on the north side, behind a perimeter fence with one gate per pen: 0.79 m wide for pen 4 and 0.82 m for pen 3; these gates were the only way out of the pens. In the middle of the back (south) side, where the radial fence starts, a tunnel 23 m long and about 4.3 m wide runs south under the west stand to the concourse behind the turnstiles, about 40 by 20 m. 3,000 people: 600 in pen 4 and 600 in pen 3, already packed, and 1,800 fans in the concourse who came in through an exit gate opened to relieve the crush outside and head down the tunnel into the pens.
cases.what_happened: After an exit gate was opened to relieve the crush at the turnstiles, about 2,000 fans came through it and many walked down the tunnel into two pens that were already full; people at the front were crushed against the perimeter fence.
cases.lesson: A full area needs its entrance closed: count people into each pen and close the route in before it is full.

sources.label: Lord Justice Taylor (1989), The Hillsborough Stadium Disaster, Interim Report, Cm 765 (tunnel 23 m and 1 in 6, gates 0.82 m and 0.79 m, about 2,000 through gate C)
HSE, G. Norton (1989), An investigation into the number of people in pens 3 and 4 (pen areas, 1,576 people in pen 3 at 15:03, 8.4 per m²)
Wikipedia, Hillsborough disaster (official death toll of 97)

dimensions: Tunnel about 23 m long, descending to the terrace at 1 in 6; the radial fence between pens 3 and 4 bisects its mouth (Taylor, para. 45).
Perimeter gates: pen 3 0.82 m, pen 4 0.79 m (Taylor, para. 260).
Pen areas about 188 m² (pen 3) and 192 m² (pen 4) from the inquiry drawing (HSE, Norton 1989, table 2).
About 2,000 came through gate C in five minutes, a large proportion into the tunnel (Taylor, para. 70).
Pen 3 held about 1,576 people at 15:03, 8.4 per m² on average (HSE, Norton 1989).
approximations: The pens are drawn as two 12.5 × 15 m rectangles; crush barriers (including the one that broke) are not drawn.
The tunnel width (4.3 m, 14 ft) comes from press reports, not from the inquiry; the concourse size is an estimate.
The terrace and the tunnel slope are drawn flat.

The simulator cannot start people denser than 4 per m², so the pens start at about 3.8 per m² (they were above 5.4 per m² by 14:50) and more arrive through the tunnel than the 1,100 or so that history suggests.
The 0.79 m gate is drawn 0.8 m (the simulator's narrowest door); the gates are open from the start (they were opened from about 15:00).

cases.title: Itaewon 2022 · Seoul alley
cases.description: Open-air streets in Itaewon, Seoul, on Halloween night, 29 October 2022, about 22:15. A sloping alley about 45 m long and 3.2 m wide at its narrowest runs north to south. Its north end meets a narrow street lined with bars at a T; draw 80 m of that street, about 6 m wide, open at its west and east ends. Its south end opens onto the main road, Itaewon-ro; draw 80 m of it, about 12 m wide, open at its west and east ends. 2,400 people: 1,200 on the upper street heading down the alley to Itaewon-ro, 400 in the alley also heading down to Itaewon-ro, and 800 on Itaewon-ro heading up the alley to the upper street.
cases.what_happened: On a Halloween night with about 100,000 people in the district, a 3.2 m alley between two packed streets filled until people fell; police estimate 8 to 11 people per m² there between 22:15 and 22:25.
cases.lesson: Narrow links between crowded streets need one-way flow and a limit on how many enter.

sources.label: Wikipedia, Seoul Halloween crowd crush (alley about 45 m long, 3.2 m at its narrowest, sloping up from Itaewon-ro; 159 deaths)
AP via The Boston Globe (13 Jan 2023), police special investigation: about 8 people per m² at 22:15, 9 to 11 at 22:25

dimensions: Alley about 45 m long and 3.2 m wide at its narrowest, sloping up from Itaewon-ro (Wikipedia, citing Korean reporting).
Density about 8 people per m² at 22:15 and 9 to 11 per m² at 22:25 (police special investigation with the National Forensic Service, via AP).
approximations: The widths of the upper street (6 m) and of Itaewon-ro (12 m), and the 80 m drawn of each, are estimates.
The alley is drawn 3.2 m wide over its whole length and flat; the slope that pushed people down is not simulated.
Who walked which way is an assumption: the sources describe packed streets pouring into the alley; here 1,600 head down and 800 head up.
2,400 people stand for the much larger crowd in the district that night.
